thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 alert — post-deploy latency oscillation detected on runtime-canary. High p99 and throughput drop. Link: https://alerts.redwood/1769937200

ashwin: Oncall here, pulling graphs now. Which rollout triggered this?

miguel: Rolling deploy v2026.03.14-hotwave to canary pool at 12:18 UTC. Saw sawtooth p50->p99 spikes starting ~12:27.

ashwin: Confirmed. p95 up x3, p99 up x7. Throughput per-pod down ~40%.

incident-bot: Logs showing frequent kernel fallback events (kernel_selector: fallback_fast_to_safe) and KV cache thrash. Sample: `kernel_fallback=true` lines flooding.

ashwin: Ask runtime team to triage kernel fallback chain. @miguel can you check kernel affinity/metrics?

miguel: On it. Initial quick grep shows `eviction_reason=kv_pool_pressure` and `batch_window` increased on switched workers. Looks like continuous batching + new scheduling policy caused prefetch fanout -> eviction -> fallback loop.

ashwin: Immediate mitigation options: 1) Flip feature-flag `hotwave-routing` to off (kill-switch) 2) Revert canary rollout 3) Reduce canary traffic/scale up. Thoughts?

dmitri: I can flip the flag now. Recommend kill-switch first to avoid broader impact. If that doesn't stabilize in 3 min, rollback.

ashwin: Do it. Patch the flag and confirm. Command: `curl -XPOST https://flags.api/kill -d '{"flag":"hotwave-routing","value":false}'`

dmitri: Done. `hotwave-routing=false` returned 200. Pushed to canary pool.

ops-bot: Flag update event: hotwave-routing=false by dmitri at 12:39:17 UTC

ashwin: Telemetry: p99 trending down but still noisy. Throughput improving slightly.

miguel: Kernel fallback count dropped ~60% after flag flip. However we still see intermittent prefetch eviction spikes for longer sequences. Preemptively throttling batch_window might help. Can we set `batch_window_ms=4` on canary?

dmitri: Can apply config via runtime-ctl. I can push a temporary lower batch window to canary nodes. Applying now.

ashwin: Apply and monitor. Command: `runtime-ctl set --selector canary --batch-window-ms 4`

dmitri: Applied. Confirmed on canary nodes.

katie: Support — any known customer impact? We have an open chat with AcmeGames complaining about slow generative responses. Should we page them?

sara: Product/CS: AcmeGames is in canary region but only 5% traffic. If kill-switch works they should see improvement. @jenn can you message them with "we're investigating a transient post-deploy regression and have applied mitigations"?

jenn: On it. Sending preliminary note now.

jenn: Message sent to AcmeGames PM: "We've detected a post-deploy latency regression; we've applied a kill-switch and config tweak. We're monitoring and will update in 15m."

ashwin: Telemetry 5m post-mitigation: p95 stable, p99 still ~2x baseline for spikes but much rarer. Throughput back to ~90% of baseline.

miguel: Root cause hypothesis: new scheduling pass in v2026.03.14-hotwave increased simultaneous prefetch fanout on longer sequences which increased KV pool pressure on certain kernel paths. That triggered fallback to safe kernels causing increased latencies and lower throughput due to less efficient kernels.

dmitri: Agreed. We saw kernel-selector choose safe kernels when eviction_count > threshold. Eviction_count trended up after the scheduling change.

ashwin: Next steps: 1) Keep flag off across release ring 2) Re-run canary with batch_window=4 and telemetry guard 3) Postmortem once stabilized. Who owns rollout revert? @miguel?

miguel: I can coordinate a trimmed rollout after we validate synthetic load. For now keep `hotwave-routing=false` global for ramp-out.

ops-bot: Feature flag event: hotwave-routing=false propagated to production rings at 12:45:59 UTC by dmitri

katie: Support: I'll hold customer comms and escalate to enterprise leads for any SLA reachouts. @sara want me to send an Incident Status update?

sara: Yes, please: Summary + mitigations + ETA for full fix (TBD). Keep wording non-technical.

ashwin: I'm going to hand off to @miguel for next-hour monitoring and postmortem. If things degrade again, page the oncall rotation. @dmitri please put a short-runbook in the incident doc for flag flip + batch_window tweak steps.

miguel: Taking over. I'll keep this channel as active log. Watching dashboards and kernel fallback metrics.

ashwin: Thanks — handing to runtime. Oncall clear for now.

miguel: Quick notes for postmortem: candidate fix paths: 1) revert scheduling policy 2) add KV pool backpressure throttle 3) make fallback threshold adaptive. Will propose patch and test in canary.

dmitri: Saved runbook snippet to incident playbook: `- flip hotwave-routing flag` `- set batch_window_ms=4 for canary` `- monitor kernel_fallback_count`

jenn: Customer update sent: "Mitigations applied; improvements observed; we will provide a full update by EOD."

ashwin: Marking incident as mitigated for now. Still in post-deploy monitoring. If any regression or customer impact resurfaces, re-open P1. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: Incident status changed: mitigated by ashwin at 13:22:45 UTC

miguel: Last note: schedule a controlled re-run of the release with adjustments and synthetic load to validate before any new ramp. I'll create a release-issue and link infra experiments.

katie: Thanks team. I'll prep the external postmortem template and coordinate CS follow-ups.

sara: Great job everyone. We'll meet for the incident review tomorrow 10:30 UTC.

jenn: Closing loop with AcmeGames once we have final remediation plan.

ashwin: Thread closed to updates; monitoring-only. If someone needs to re-open, ping @oncall."
